entries.name: Anthropic Agent Skills (official)
entries.claimed_description: Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks; includes the document skills that power Claude's file creation.
entries.actual_functionality: 19 skill folders (SKILL.md plus helper scripts). None covers e-commerce, marketplaces, listings, reviews or digital shelf. Relevant to us: xlsx, pdf, docx and pptx (each 8-17 Python/JS helper scripts, bundled OOXML schemas, LibreOffice-based recalculation and validation), skill-creator (authoring guide plus an evaluation harness), mcp-builder, webapp-testing (Playwright). brand-guidelines is 73 lines about Anthropic's own brand only. README: the skills are "for demonstration and educational purposes only".
entries.licence_note: No root LICENSE file. 18 of 19 skills carry a LICENSE.txt with the Apache-2.0 text (doc-coauthoring has none; the docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx copies leave the copyright placeholder unfilled). THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists GPL-3.0 FFmpeg, pulled in by imageio-ffmpeg for the slack-gif-creator skill only.
entries.popularity_note: about 201k GitHub stars; 469 open issues; no tagged releases (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Scripts start local processes (subprocess calls to LibreOffice; webapp-testing/with_server.py uses shell=True for a caller-supplied server command; skill-creator shells out to the claude CLI). No unexpected network hosts in the document skills. No injection-style instructions or zero-width characters found in SKILL.md files; the few HTML comments are code-sample placeholders.
entries.verdict_reason: Official and Apache-2.0 but generic: reuse the spreadsheet/PDF/slide skills for report generation and skill-creator as the template for our own e-commerce skills.
entries.fit_in_engine: Reporting agent (Excel, PDF, PowerPoint outputs); authoring standard and evaluation harness for in-house skills.

entries.name: Amazon SP-API samples (official SP-API MCP servers, A+ Content Manager, listings app)
entries.claimed_description: Sample code in various programming languages for use cases supported by the Amazon Selling Partner API, including developer tools (MCP servers and a local sandbox) and code recipes.
entries.actual_functionality: (1) sp-api-dev-mcp: two local MCP servers, published to npm as @amazon-sp-api-release/sp-api-dev-mcp v1.0.5 - a Developer Assistant (6 tools: documentation search with local embeddings, endpoint catalogue, live sp_api_execute, code generation, Orders API migration, code review; TypeScript with 27 test files) and a Workflow builder (26 tools listed in its README). (2) Data Kiosk MCP server for seller and vendor analytics (GraphQL). (3) A local AI sandbox that validates requests against the OpenAPI schemas. (4) A+ Content Manager: React + Node app (120 files) covering Standard, Premium and Brand Story documents and 39 module types, with validation and a credential-free sample mode. (5) Listings sample application in Next.js 14 / TypeScript (373 files). (6) Code recipes in Java, Python and PHP. README: these are "not supported products in their own right, but educational examples".
entries.licence_note: Root LICENSE is MIT No Attribution. The MCP sub-packages declare Apache-2.0 in package.json (npm shows Apache-2.0 too). Both are permissive; the mismatch is cosmetic.
entries.popularity_note: about 223 GitHub stars; 3 open issues; latest release tag mcp-server-v1.0.5; npm @amazon-sp-api-release/sp-api-dev-mcp 1,868 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: sp_api_execute accepts GET, POST, PUT and DELETE with the seller credentials held in environment variables - an agent could change listings or prices, and no confirmation gate was seen. A clone-repo helper accepts a caller-supplied repository URL and target path. The documentation search downloads an embedding model (Xenova/multilingual-e5-small, whose model card declares no licence) from Hugging Face on first use and crawls developer-docs.amazon.com. Only Amazon, GitHub and Hugging Face hosts were found in the assistant source.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Amazon SP-API (Login with Amazon client id/secret and refresh token; seller or vendor account; A+ Content needs Brand Registry; Data Kiosk needs the relevant role). Amazon announced SP-API fees for third-party developers from 2026 - whether a brand owner's private app is exempt was not verified in this session.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Uses the official APIs, which is the compliant route. Amazon's Acceptable Use Policy and Data Protection Policy still govern what may be passed to AI tools (the Data Kiosk README says so explicitly).
entries.verdict_reason: Official and permissively licensed: take the Next.js listings sample, the A+ module catalogue and validator, and the recipes as starting code; give engineers the developer MCP with read-only credentials.
entries.fit_in_engine: Marketplace connector layer (listings, A+ Content, catalogue, Data Kiosk analytics); developer tooling.

entries.name: Nexscope Amazon Skills
entries.claimed_description: 52 free AI agent skills built for Amazon sellers - keyword research, listing optimization, FBA calculations, PPC campaigns and more. "No binaries, no API keys".
entries.actual_functionality: 52 SKILL.md files, about 11,600 lines. The listing-optimization skill (about 300 lines) has a create mode and an audit mode with an 8-dimension, 100-point rubric; a-plus-content is 504 lines, listing-images 421, review-analyzer 162 (a report template with no data-collection method). Six scripts: three bash scrapers that fetch Amazon product pages (12 country sites) with a spoofed Chrome User-Agent and call Amazon's undocumented autocomplete endpoint, and three offline Python calculators (FBA fees, tariffs). All 52 skill files link to the vendor's paid product; review-analyzer scripts a marketing sentence for the agent to say. The listing-images skill contradicts itself (main image "2000px minimum" and "minimum 1000px").
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2026 Nexscope AI.
entries.popularity_note: about 907 GitHub stars; 1 open issue; README badge claims "12K+ downloads" (unverified) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: amazon-keyword-research/scripts/research.sh pastes the user's keyword into python3 -c "...quote('$KEYWORD')" - a crafted keyword can execute arbitrary Python (code injection). The scraping scripts make requests to Amazon sites from whatever machine runs the agent. Skills embed tracking links and vendor upsell text into agent output (commercial bias). No hidden instructions or zero-width characters found.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None required; repeatedly upsells Nexscope's paid MCP and API.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: fetch-listing.sh and fetch-competitor.sh scrape Amazon detail pages while impersonating a browser, with no robots.txt check. Amazon's Conditions of Use restrict automated data collection (wording not re-read in this session) - do not run these scripts.
entries.verdict_reason: Some usable rubric ideas, but the scraping scripts, an injection bug and built-in vendor promotion make it unsafe to install as-is.
entries.fit_in_engine: Idea source for listing-audit scoring dimensions, each to be re-verified against Amazon's own style guides.

entries.name: Nexscope eCommerce Skills
entries.claimed_description: Free AI agent skills for Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, TikTok Shop and Walmart sellers.
entries.actual_functionality: 162 SKILL.md files. 114 are shorter than 70 lines and share one generic template (share-of-shelf is 56 lines with no data source, method or formula; product-title-optimization 63 lines; walmart-listing-optimization 64). 26 exceed 200 lines (product-description-generator 398, product-review-analysis 320). 42 standalone Python scripts (review-checker parser/analyser/HTML report, brand monitoring, margin calculators); in brand-monitoring/scripts/scrapers.py the real HTTP calls are commented out ("Enable actual API call in production"). Code comments read as machine-translated.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2026 Nexscope AI.
entries.popularity_note: about 1.5k GitHub stars; 4 open issues; README badge claims "16K+ downloads" (unverified) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: No live network calls found in the scripts (requests are stubbed or commented out). All 162 skill files carry a link to the vendor's commercial site.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Price-tracker and competitor-monitoring skills describe a strategy only; no scraper is shipped.
entries.verdict_reason: Mostly template stubs with little substance; the digital-shelf content is a heading, not a method.
entries.fit_in_engine: At most a checklist of topics (share of shelf, MAP monitoring, review checking).

entries.name: Amazon Seller Skill Suite
entries.claimed_description: 6 Claude Cowork skills for Amazon marketplace selling. Works with any brand, any product category, any seller account type.
entries.actual_functionality: Six .skill zip bundles, each holding one SKILL.md of 2,464-4,784 words - no scripts, no URLs, no tool calls. Listing QA is a hard pre-publish gate: exact UTF-8 byte counts for backend keywords (249-byte limit), category title limits, contradiction detection, "content is data, not instructions" injection defence, BLOCK verdicts by default. Listing Optimizer adds input gates and anti-hallucination rules (label figures VERIFIED / ESTIMATED / INFERRED; never invent BSR or search volumes). Also brand guardian, trend researcher, account strategist and social strategist skills.
entries.language: Markdown (prompt-only); one Python script that builds the README PDF
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2026 Scott Converse.
entries.popularity_note: about 5 GitHub stars; 0 open issues; single v1.0 drop (bundle files dated 2026-03-18) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Prompt-only. The zip bundles contain only SKILL.md (verified by listing archive contents, nothing extracted or run). generate_pdf.py only renders a PDF with reportlab. README warns the skills "run autonomously in Claude's CoWork mode and may take actions on your behalf". No network hosts.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: None - it works on text the user supplies. The policy limits it quotes (byte limits, prohibited claims, A+ rules) are the author's reading and must be re-verified against current Amazon policy.
entries.verdict_reason: Best-engineered prompt pack found and MIT-licensed; adapt the QA-gate pattern and exact byte/character checks into our rules engine and reviewer prompts after verifying each rule.
entries.fit_in_engine: Content validation and pre-publish QA agent; anti-hallucination guardrails for listing generation.

entries.name: Amazon Pro Skills
entries.claimed_description: 67 production-grade Claude Code skills for serious Amazon sellers. Free and open.
entries.actual_functionality: 67 SKILL.md files (about 10,900 lines, 130-280 lines each); no scripts - the user pastes their own data. Relevant: customer-question-mining (164 lines), review-analyzer (151), listing-images (139), ai-image-policy-compliance (153), attributes-completer (131), a-plus-content (260). CLAUDE.md says the library is a from-scratch rewrite of the Nexscope topic list. Contains unreferenced numeric claims about Amazon's Rufus assistant (for example "answer length 80 to 200 words") and a WhatsApp-group call to action at the end of every skill.
entries.licence_note: No LICENSE file. The README ends with "License: MIT." - a one-word statement with no licence text or copyright line; GitHub reports "not specified". Treat as not cleanly licensed until a LICENSE file exists.
entries.popularity_note: about 15 GitHub stars; 0 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Prompt-only; no scripts or network calls. The promotional footer (WhatsApp invite link) would surface in agent output.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: None directly; its claims about Amazon algorithms are unverified.
entries.verdict_reason: No licence file and unverifiable claims; read for ideas only (customer Q&A mining loop, AI-image policy checklist).
entries.fit_in_engine: Idea source for Q&A mining and attribute-completeness features.

entries.name: Amazon Marketing Skill
entries.claimed_description: An open-source Claude Code skill for Amazon product listing optimization, keyword strategy, and content marketing. No paid dependencies.
entries.actual_functionality: Router SKILL.md plus six sub-skills (listing-optimizer 335 lines, a-plus-content 368, product-onboarding 285, keyword-research 192, competitor-analysis 159, listing-audit 149), three reference guides (a 270-line style guide citing Amazon rules "last verified April 2026", backend keywords, Rufus optimisation) and five templates (audit scorecard, keyword map, listing brief, product and brand context). The listing audit is an explicit compliance checklist for title, bullets, description and backend keywords plus a 100-point quality score. Product onboarding tells the agent to capture Amazon pages with Playwright and explicitly forbids anti-bot evasion and login-gated access. It states there are "17 module types" for A+ Content, while Amazon's own sample app lists 39 - the rules need checking.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, "copyright (c) 2026 contributors".
entries.popularity_note: about 3 GitHub stars; 0 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Prompt-only, no scripts. No promotional content or hidden instructions found.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None (optional Playwright MCP for page capture).
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Product onboarding fetches Amazon detail pages through browser automation; even without evasion this is automated collection from Amazon. Use SP-API Catalog/Listings data for own ASINs instead.
entries.verdict_reason: Clean MIT prompt set with the clearest compliance checklist and scorecard; adapt after verifying each rule and replacing page capture with SP-API data.
entries.fit_in_engine: Listing-audit scoring model; seed list of content rules for the validation engine.

entries.name: Claude Office Skills
entries.claimed_description: A curated collection of practical Claude Skills for real-world office tasks. Zero setup required. 136+ skills and an Office MCP server with 39 tools.
entries.actual_functionality: About 140 skill folders. The e-commerce ones (amazon-seller 514 lines, shopify-automation, woocommerce-automation) are pseudo-YAML "automation" templates that name an ecommerce-mcp server and tools (amazon_sp_api, amazon_ads_api and others) found nowhere in the repository. Real code exists only for the office-mcp document server (TypeScript, with a committed dist/ build).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2026 Claude Office Skills Contributors. Not an Anthropic project despite the name.
entries.popularity_note: about 597 GitHub stars; 3 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: README promotes piping install.sh from the internet into bash. office-mcp depends on npm xlsx ^0.18.5 (the npm registry copy stops at 0.18.5) and on pdf-lib, unmaintained since 2021. Skills describe automations such as auto-repricing and review requests with nothing implemented - an agent would have to improvise.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Mentions Helium 10, Jungle Scout and SP-API; none is implemented.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Describes automated review requests and repricing without reference to marketplace policy.
entries.verdict_reason: The e-commerce skills point at tooling that does not exist; nothing reusable for us.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: Marketing Skills (Corey Haines)
entries.claimed_description: A collection of AI agent skills focused on marketing tasks - conversion optimization, copywriting, SEO, analytics, and growth engineering.
entries.actual_functionality: 53 skills (version 2.14.28), typically 190-500 lines each with reference files; 69 small command-line wrappers for third-party marketing APIs; validation scripts, tests and evals; a written sponsorship policy ("sponsorship funds the work, never the recommendations") with paying partners marked in the text. Oriented to SaaS/B2B marketing: almost nothing on marketplaces or product listings. Relevant frameworks: copywriting, copy-editing, schema (structured data), ai-seo, customer-research (review mining), competitor-profiling.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2025 Corey Haines.
entries.popularity_note: about 63k GitHub stars; 46 open issues; release v2.14.28 in the week of inspection (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: The CLI wrappers call many third-party SaaS APIs with user-supplied keys (not needed to use the skills). README and some skills name paying partners (disclosed). One compiled .pyc file is committed. Phrase scan for injection-style instructions returned only benign hits.
entries.verdict_reason: High-quality MIT prompt library: lift the copywriting, SEO, schema and customer-research frameworks and drop the SaaS-specific and partner sections.
entries.fit_in_engine: Copy-quality and SEO reasoning prompts for brand-site and retailer content; method for mining review themes.

entries.name: Anthropic Knowledge Work Plugins
entries.claimed_description: Plugins that turn Claude into a specialist for your role, team, and company.
entries.actual_functionality: Role plugins made of SKILL.md files and MCP connector configs. Marketing plugin: 8 skills (brand-review 276 lines, competitive-brief 331, performance-report 392, seo-audit 190, content-creation, draft-content, campaign-plan, email-sequence). partner-built/brand-voice (by Tribe AI): discover-brand, guideline-generation and brand-voice-enforcement skills plus agent definitions. entries.popularity_note: about 37k GitHub stars; 98 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: The .mcp.json files connect to third-party hosted MCP servers by default - review before enabling any. No injection-style instructions found in the marketing or brand-voice skills.

entries.verdict_reason: Official and permissive; brand-review and brand-voice-enforcement map directly onto brand-guideline compliance checks.

entries.name: amazon_sp_mcp (jay-trivedi)
entries.claimed_description: MCP server that provides AI agents with access to Amazon Seller Central data through SP-API - sales, returns, inventory, listings, reports.
entries.actual_functionality: About 1,100 lines of TypeScript for credentials, token management, request signing, a rate limiter and an HTTP client, with unit tests - but src/index.ts registers a single "hello" tool. None of the advertised data tools exists.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2025 Jay Trivedi.

entries.name: amazon-seller-mcp (MarceauSolutions)
entries.claimed_description: AI-powered Amazon Seller Central tools for inventory management, fee calculation, and optimization via SP-API.
entries.actual_functionality: Eight files, about 2,000 lines of Python: an MCP server with 8 tools over the python-amazon-sp-api library (inventory, orders, product details) plus offline FBA-fee and restock calculators. The README describes directories (src/, mcp-server/, SKILL.md, CHANGELOG) that are absent, and the wheel configuration points at a non-existent src/ path.
entries.licence_note: No LICENSE file. pyproject.toml and README say MIT; GitHub reports "not specified".
entries.popularity_note: about 6 GitHub stars; PyPI amazon-seller-mcp 173 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Caches API responses (which can include order data) in local JSON files; dependency floors only, no lock file; no tests.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Order data is personal data under Amazon's Data Protection Policy; local caching would need controls.
entries.verdict_reason: No licence file, inconsistent packaging and no tests; nothing the official SDK does not already give us.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: Amazon SP-API MCP (Ailumia)
entries.claimed_description: A production-grade, version-aware MCP server for the Amazon Selling Partner API: six tools over 353 operations across 49 API domains.
entries.actual_functionality: About 3,500 lines of TypeScript including 10 test files, CI, CodeQL, dependabot, SECURITY.md and a written security model. Tools: list_accounts, discover_operations, describe_operation, invoke_operation, get_artifact, run_report. The registry holds 353 operations (verified by counting registry/operations.json), generated from amzn/selling-partner-api-models. Writes and deletes are refused unless confirm=true or dryRun is set (verified in src/execution/sp-api-executor.ts); credentials come only from the server environment; requests are schema-validated; the HTTP transport binds to loopback by default.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0, with NOTICE. Independent project, not affiliated with Amazon.
entries.popularity_note: about 4 GitHub stars; npm 16 downloads/week; v1.0.0 released 2026-07-20 (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Sound design: confirmation gate, schema validation, audit events with payload hashes, no caller-set headers. The authors state the limits themselves: confirmation is not authorisation; one process must not serve mutually untrusted tenants; downloaded artifacts are stored unencrypted. Very new and almost unused, so no independent scrutiny yet.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Official API route. Agent access to seller data must still follow Amazon's Acceptable Use and Data Protection policies.
entries.verdict_reason: The best-built community SP-API MCP server and permissively licensed, but unproven: pilot only with a read-only SP-API role and a pinned version.
entries.fit_in_engine: Analyst or agent access to SP-API reports and catalogue data; alternative to writing our own MCP wrapper.

entries.name: amazon-sp-mcp (mansournorouzi)
entries.claimed_description: MCP server that connects Claude to Amazon Seller Central via the SP-API: natural-language queries for sales, inventory, reports, fees, reimbursements and analytics.
entries.actual_functionality: About 2,700 lines of TypeScript; 20 read-only tools implemented (orders, inventory, sales metrics, financial events, catalogue search, settlement/fee/storage reports, Sales and Traffic report, Brand Analytics search-terms report, inventory ledger) with report polling and CSV parsing. Login-with-Amazon auth only. jest is configured but there is no tests directory; six ad-hoc test-*.mjs scripts sit in the root.
entries.licence_note: No LICENSE file. package.json and README say MIT; GitHub reports "not specified".
entries.popularity_note: about 53 GitHub stars; 2 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: The README carries a notice that the axios npm package was compromised on 2026-03-31 (malicious versions 1.14.1 and 0.30.4) and pins axios to 1.14.0 - a reminder to pin and lock dependencies everywhere. test-debug.mjs prints the full token response to the console. The read-only tool set limits the damage an agent could do.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Official API route; order tools return buyer data.
entries.verdict_reason: Useful worked examples of report polling and Brand Analytics retrieval, but no licence file and no tests.
entries.fit_in_engine: Reference for ingesting search-terms and sales/traffic reports.

entries.name: Shopify AI Toolkit (official)
entries.claimed_description: Connect your AI tools to the Shopify platform: documentation, API schemas, code validation, and store management through the CLI.
entries.actual_functionality: Official Shopify plugin (version 2.5.0) for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others: two skills (shopify - a 126-line router with about 170 reference and asset files including compressed Admin API schemas for five API versions; ucp - 330 lines for the Universal Commerce Protocol CLI that can search, cart and buy), validation scripts (GraphQL, Liquid themes, Functions, UI components) and telemetry hooks. The .mcp.json is empty: this is a skills bundle, not an MCP server. Older per-topic skills sit in deprecated/. The separately named Shopify/dev-mcp repository could not be cloned (see Not inspected).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2025-present Shopify Inc.
entries.popularity_note: about 654 GitHub stars; 25 open issues; npm @shopify/ai-toolkit 613 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Installs hooks on every user prompt and tool use that POST usage events to https://shopify.dev/mcp/usage; on Claude Code up to the first 2,000 characters of the user's prompt are attached when a Shopify skill activates (hooks/scripts/track-telemetry.sh). On by default; opt out with OPT_OUT_INSTRUMENTATION=true, DO_NOT_TRACK or an opt-out file. The SKILL.md tells the agent that every response must run a logging script. 93 compressed data files (API schemas) are bundled.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Shopify partner or store account for store operations.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Official tooling. The ucp skill can place orders - not something a brand-intelligence agent should be allowed to do.
entries.verdict_reason: Official and MIT, but aimed at Shopify app developers; only relevant if a Shopify direct-to-consumer store joins scope, and then with telemetry switched off.
entries.fit_in_engine: Possible future connector reference for a Shopify brand store.

entries.name: mcp-walmart-ads (Walmart Ads + Marketplace, community)
entries.claimed_description: MCP server for three Walmart Inc. API families behind one tool surface - four tools over 31 APIs and 424 operations.
entries.actual_functionality: About 3,800 lines of Python 3.13 with 10 test files, CI and a spec-drift workflow; bundles Walmart's OpenAPI specifications (33 JSON files); four tools: list_endpoints, describe_endpoint, call_endpoint (generic proxy) and download_file. Handles RSA-SHA256 request signing and OAuth client credentials. A community project by one maintainer. Our search found no official Walmart MCP server.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2026 Jon X.
entries.popularity_note: about 3 GitHub stars; PyPI 473 downloads/month; version 0.5.1 (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: call_endpoint is a generic proxy flagged as destructive (it can change items, prices and campaigns) with no confirmation step. The private key and tokens are read from a local config file. Single maintainer.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Walmart Marketplace or Walmart Connect API credentials (US third-party seller or ads partner).
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Official API route; Walmart API terms apply.
entries.verdict_reason: Competent but tiny community project for a marketplace that may not be in scope; there is no official Walmart MCP server to prefer.
entries.fit_in_engine: Reference if Walmart US is added later.

entries.name: Amazon Ads MCP (Kuudo / Openbridge)
entries.claimed_description: Open-source Amazon Ads MCP server: 711 Amazon Ads API operations across 53 services, with read and write tools.
entries.actual_functionality: Large Python project (275 .py files, about 150 unit/integration test files, CI, Docker, version 0.3.33) built on FastMCP; generates tools from bundled Amazon Ads OpenAPI specs (220 JSON files). Auth modes: direct (own Amazon Ads API credentials) or brokered through the vendor's services. Published by Kuudo, an Openbridge company - not Amazon. Amazon's own Ads MCP server is a hosted open beta for API partners; no Amazon GitHub repository for it was found.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2024 KuudoAI.
entries.popularity_note: about 75 GitHub stars; PyPI 952 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Read and write tools for live advertising accounts. AUTH_METHOD=openbridge or kuudo routes tokens through third-party hosts (authentication.api.openbridge.io) - use "direct" only. Depends on the openai SDK. A custom build backend runs repository code at build time.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Amazon Ads API access (approved API credentials); optional vendor-hosted services (pricing not checked).
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Official API route; Amazon Ads API licence terms apply.
entries.verdict_reason: Advertising control sits outside the digital-shelf content scope; revisit for share-of-voice and ads reporting.
entries.fit_in_engine: Later phase: sponsored share of voice and ads performance ingestion.

entries.name: Firecrawl MCP Server
entries.claimed_description: Firecrawl MCP server: search, scrape, parse, crawl, map, and interact with the web. Works with Firecrawl cloud or a self-hosted instance.
entries.actual_functionality: About 9,900 lines of TypeScript (version 3.41.0) with tests and Docker; a client over the Firecrawl API (scrape, crawl, map, search, extract/agent, credit usage). Works against Firecrawl cloud (API key; a keyless tier covers scrape, search and parse with rate limits) or a self-hosted instance via FIRECRAWL_API_URL.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2025 vrknetha. The Firecrawl server it talks to is AGPL-3.0 (separate entry).
entries.popularity_note: about 7.9k GitHub stars; npm firecrawl-mcp 106,077 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: All page content passes through a third-party cloud unless self-hosted. A prepare script builds the package when installed from git.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Firecrawl cloud (credit-based paid plans; limited keyless free tier) or a self-hosted Firecrawl.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Firecrawl's README says it respects robots.txt by default and leaves compliance with site terms to the user. Marketplace pages remain off-limits for scraping.
entries.verdict_reason: Convenient for ad-hoc research on permitted sites, but it adds a paid third party and is not needed in the engine core.
entries.fit_in_engine: Optional research tool for public brand and retailer pages.

entries.name: Apify MCP Server
entries.claimed_description: Connect your agent to the largest marketplace of tools for AI.
entries.actual_functionality: About 28,000 lines of TypeScript, 180 test files, version 0.23.0. Tools to search Apify Store, read an Actor's input schema and pricing, run Actors and read result datasets. Hosted at mcp.apify.com or run locally.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: MIT, copyright 2025 Apify.
entries.popularity_note: about 18k GitHub stars; npm @apify/actors-mcp-server 34,764 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Telemetry (Segment and Sentry) is on by default; opt out with TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false. It runs third-party Actors written by independent developers - each is separate code with its own behaviour and price.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Apify account and token; pay-per-use Actors (prices vary per Actor).
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Many Store Actors scrape Amazon, Walmart and similar sites on your behalf - the terms-of-use risk stays with the customer.
entries.verdict_reason: Fine for sanctioned public-web research; marketplace Actors must not become a data source for the engine.
entries.fit_in_engine: Optional, off-core research channel.

entries.name: Bright Data MCP
entries.claimed_description: The Bright Data MCP server gives AI agents real-time access to public web data (30 tools).
entries.actual_functionality: About 3,400 lines of JavaScript (version 4.10.0) with 29 test files: web search, page fetch as Markdown, a catalogue of pre-built scrapers (README names products and search results from Amazon, Walmart, eBay and Etsy, and Walmart reviews) and remote browser control. At start-up it checks the customer's Bright Data account and creates "unblocker" and browser zones if they are missing. It wraps scraped content in random-nonce "untrusted" markers before returning it to the model, as a prompt-injection defence.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2025 Bright Data.
entries.popularity_note: about 2.7k GitHub stars; npm @brightdata/mcp 15,641 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: All traffic goes through Bright Data's network with your API token. An old packaged bundle (brightdata-mcp-2.7.1.mcpb, a zip) is committed next to the 4.10.0 source. The untrusted-content wrapping is a good practice worth copying.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Bright Data account. README: 5,000 free requests per month, then $1.50 per 1,000 results and $8 per GB for browser sessions.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Built to get past site blocking. Collecting Amazon or Walmart pages this way conflicts with those sites' terms and with a brand owner's own seller or vendor agreements.
entries.verdict_reason: Its main use is anti-blocking scraping of marketplaces; the terms and legal exposure outweigh the convenience.
entries.fit_in_engine: None (borrow the untrusted-content wrapping idea only).

entries.name: Playwright MCP (Microsoft)
entries.claimed_description: MCP server that provides browser automation capabilities using Playwright, through structured accessibility snapshots.
entries.actual_functionality: A thin package (44 files, version 0.0.86) exposing the MCP server implemented inside Playwright; it depends on an alpha build of Playwright (1.66.0-alpha-2026-11-18). Options for isolated profiles, origin allow and block lists, and a secrets file.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0 (Microsoft).
entries.popularity_note: about 40k GitHub stars; npm @playwright/mcp about 10.7 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: The README states that the origin allow/block lists do "not serve as a security boundary". A browsing agent can be steered by page content (prompt injection) and can act with any logged-in session - use isolated profiles and never seller-account sessions. Tracks alpha Playwright builds.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: The tool is neutral; pointing it at marketplaces or at a logged-in Seller Central would breach their terms.
entries.verdict_reason: Trusted vendor and licence; adopt as an internal QA and development tool (testing our own app, checking our own brand site), not as a data collector.
entries.fit_in_engine: Engineering QA; visual checks of brand-site pages.

entries.name: awesome-mcp-servers (punkpeye)
entries.claimed_description: A curated list of awesome Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
entries.actual_functionality: One README of links with one-line descriptions, including an E-Commerce section of 50 entries. The Amazon and Walmart entries are mostly wrappers around commercial scraping or data APIs, or small community SP-API servers. No official Amazon or Walmart retail MCP server appears.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT (covers the list, not the linked projects).
entries.popularity_note: about 99k GitHub stars (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Inclusion is not vetting: entries are community-submitted and not audited. Two listed servers we inspected were unfinished (jay-trivedi) or had no licence file (MarceauSolutions).
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Many listed e-commerce servers depend on scraping vendors.
entries.verdict_reason: Discovery aid only; every listed server needs its own inspection.
entries.fit_in_engine: Periodic re-scan for new official marketplace servers.

entries.name: awesome-agent-skills (VoltAgent)
entries.claimed_description: A collection of official Agent Skills from leading development teams and the community. Hand-picked, not AI-slop generated.

entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT (covers the list only).
entries.popularity_note: about 38k GitHub stars (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Links point partly to a third-party registry site rather than to source repositories.
entries.verdict_reason: Discovery aid; confirms that vendor-official e-commerce skills are scarce.
entries.fit_in_engine: Periodic re-scan.

entries.name: awesome-claude-skills (ComposioHQ)
entries.claimed_description: A curated list of 1000+ production-ready Claude Skills and Plugins.
entries.actual_functionality: README (503 lines) plus 832 composio-skills folders: 732 of them are exactly 91 lines long and 795 mention the vendor's hosted "Rube MCP". The amazon-automation skill is 91 lines of generic template text telling the agent to add the vendor's hosted "Rube MCP" endpoint and discover tools there. The README links a "Shopify Automation" skill at a path that does not exist in the repository. Also includes copies of several Anthropic example skills.
entries.licence_note: No root LICENSE file; README says Apache-2.0; a few sub-folders carry their own LICENSE.txt. GitHub reports "not specified".

entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Depends on what the broker does with marketplace accounts - not inspectable.

entries.fit_in_engine: None beyond discovery.

entries.security_observations: None (links only).
