entries.name: MCP reference servers
entries.claimed_description: A collection of reference implementations for the Model Context Protocol.
entries.actual_functionality: Seven reference servers: everything, fetch, filesystem, git, memory, sequentialthinking, time. Earlier servers (PostgreSQL, Google Drive, Brave Search and others) have moved to a separate archived repository. The fetch server obeys robots.txt for model-initiated requests and refuses private and loopback addresses by default.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE describes a transition from MIT to Apache-2.0: new contributions are Apache-2.0, older ones stay MIT until relicensed; documentation is CC-BY-4.0. GitHub cannot classify it.
entries.popularity_note: about 92k GitHub stars; release v2.5.0 (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: The fetch README warns that the server can reach internal addresses when its allow flag is set. Reference quality, not hardened products.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: fetch honours robots.txt by default - the right default to copy.
entries.verdict_reason: Use as patterns (robots.txt handling, address filtering) when building our own MCP layer.
entries.fit_in_engine: Design reference for an in-house MCP server.

entries.name: Crawlee
entries.claimed_description: The scalable web crawling and scraping library for JavaScript/Node.js. "Helps you build reliable scrapers. Fast."
entries.actual_functionality: Large monorepo (3,038 files) with unit, integration and end-to-end test workflows. Packages for HTTP/Cheerio, Playwright and Puppeteer crawlers, request queues, autoscaling, sessions and proxy rotation, datasets and key-value storage. The default branch is version 4.0.0 in development (Node 22.13 or newer); the published stable line is 3.18.x. README advertises TLS-fingerprint replication and "human-like fingerprints"; the browser pool sets useFingerprints to true by default, and respectRobotsTxtFile defaults to false (both verified in source).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: Apache-2.0.
entries.popularity_note: about 27k GitHub stars; 86 open issues; npm crawlee 192,094 downloads/week; latest release v3.18.2 (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: No install-time scripts in the published packages inspected. Runs a real browser against untrusted pages - isolate the worker. Fingerprint spoofing and proxy rotation are built in and partly on by default.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Neutral tool, but its defaults lean towards evading bot detection. For compliant use set respectRobotsTxtFile: true, turn fingerprint generation off, identify the crawler honestly and keep it to sites whose terms allow it (own brand site, consenting retailers, public pages without anti-automation terms).
entries.verdict_reason: Best fit for a TypeScript stack, permissive licence, very active; configure it conservatively.
entries.fit_in_engine: Crawl workers for brand-site and permitted retailer pages (content capture for the digital-shelf audit).

entries.name: Scrapy
entries.claimed_description: A web scraping framework to extract structured data from websites; cross-platform, requires Python 3.11+, maintained by Zyte and many other contributors.
entries.actual_functionality: Version 2.20.0. 734 files with an extensive tests directory and CI. Asynchronous crawling engine, selectors, item pipelines, feed exports, robots.txt middleware (ROBOTSTXT_OBEY is False in library defaults but True in the generated project template - verified in source), auto-throttle.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: BSD 3-Clause (Scrapy developers).
entries.popularity_note: about 66k GitHub stars; 99 open issues; PyPI about 3.7 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Dependency floors rather than pins - lock versions in our build. No telemetry found.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Neutral tool; keep ROBOTSTXT_OBEY on and set an honest User-Agent.
entries.verdict_reason: Proven and permissive; the natural choice if crawl workers are written in Python.
entries.fit_in_engine: Python crawl workers (alternative to Crawlee) feeding extruct/price-parser.

entries.name: Playwright
entries.claimed_description: A framework for web automation and testing. It drives Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with a single API.
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (3,157 files; licence, manifest and README only). Repository version 1.66.0-next; npm latest 1.65.1. Browser builds are downloaded separately by its install command.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0, with NOTICE (Microsoft).
entries.popularity_note: about 101k GitHub stars; 28 open issues; npm about 178 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Downloads large browser binaries. Run browsers in a sandboxed container and never reuse logged-in marketplace sessions.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Neutral tool. Automating logged-in Seller Central/Vendor Central or bypassing CAPTCHAs would breach marketplace terms.
entries.verdict_reason: Industry standard, permissive licence, backed by Microsoft.
entries.fit_in_engine: Page rendering and screenshots for content audits; end-to-end tests of our own application.

entries.name: Crawl4AI
entries.claimed_description: Open-source LLM-friendly web crawler and scraper; "the Apache-2.0 crawler that powers Crawl4AI Cloud".
entries.actual_functionality: Version 0.9.6 (2026-11-20); 1,007 files with tests and a Docker API server. Produces Markdown from pages, with extraction strategies and LLM integration. Depends on patchright (a patched Playwright) and playwright-stealth; README lists "stealth mode" and an "undetected-browser adapter"; check_robots_txt defaults to False. Its SECURITY.md records, for 2026 alone, several critical issues in the Docker API server (pre-authentication remote code execution, a hard-coded default JWT secret, SSRF, file write) and a "PyPI supply-chain compromise of the litellm dependency", after which it switched to its own fork, unclecode-litellm, pinned to 1.81.13.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE is the Apache-2.0 text with an added "Attribution Requirement" section: public uses and distributions must display a credit line to the author. That is an extra condition beyond standard Apache-2.0.
entries.popularity_note: about 88k GitHub stars; 56 open issues; PyPI about 1.7 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: History of critical vulnerabilities in the bundled Docker API server (all listed as fixed). Depends on the project author's own fork of LiteLLM. Stealth/undetected-browser features exist to defeat bot detection.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None for crawling; optional LLM provider keys.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Stealth mode and the undetected browser are designed to bypass anti-automation controls - using them on marketplaces or retailers would violate their terms.
entries.verdict_reason: Capable, but the security history, forked dependency, attribution rider and stealth focus make Crawlee/Scrapy the safer base.
entries.fit_in_engine: None in the core; its page-to-Markdown approach is a useful reference.

entries.name: Firecrawl
entries.claimed_description: A web data API that turns websites into clean Markdown or structured data for AI (search, scrape, crawl, map, agent); cloud or self-hosted.
entries.actual_functionality: Large monorepo (1,493 files): TypeScript API and workers, a Playwright service, SDKs in several languages. Self-hosting (SELF_HOST.md) runs the API and workers plus Playwright, Redis, RabbitMQ, a PostgreSQL queue and FoundationDB; the vendor's proprietary "Fire-engine" is not included and AI features need your own model provider.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: GNU Affero GPL v3 (the repository does not say "only" or "or later"). README: SDKs and some UI components are MIT (apps/js-sdk declares MIT). Strong network copyleft: if we modify the server and let users interact with it over a network, we must offer them our modified source.
entries.popularity_note: about 211k GitHub stars; 144 open issues; latest server release v2.11.0 (June 2026); npm SDK about 1.6 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Wide dependency surface (57 direct dependencies in the API app). Admin and queue endpoints must be kept private (the self-host guide says so).
entries.external_api_dependencies: Firecrawl cloud is paid (credits); self-hosting needs your own infrastructure and optional LLM keys.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: README: respects robots.txt by default; responsibility for site policies rests with the user.
entries.verdict_reason: AGPL plus a heavy self-hosted footprint; Crawlee and Playwright cover the need under permissive licences.
entries.fit_in_engine: None in the core.

entries.name: extruct
entries.claimed_description: A library for extracting embedded metadata from HTML markup.
entries.actual_functionality: About 13 source modules, one per syntax (JSON-LD, W3C Microdata, RDFa via rdflib, Open Graph, Microformats via mf2py, Dublin Core) plus a "uniform" normaliser and a command-line tool; 10 test modules with HTML fixtures. Works on HTML you already have - it does no crawling. changedetection.io uses it for product price and stock detection (seen in that repo).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: BSD 3-Clause (Scrapinghub/Zyte).
entries.popularity_note: about 986 GitHub stars; 26 open issues; PyPI about 1.08 million downloads/month; latest release 0.18.0 (November 2024) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Unpinned dependencies - lock them. Parses untrusted HTML with lxml; changedetection.io isolates it in a subprocess because of lxml memory growth.
entries.verdict_reason: Exactly the schema.org Product/Offer/AggregateRating extractor we need; permissive and widely used.
entries.fit_in_engine: Structured-data extraction and schema.org completeness checks on brand-site and retailer pages (Python worker).

entries.name: price-parser
entries.claimed_description: Extract price and currency from a raw string.
entries.actual_functionality: Three small source files (about 2,200 lines including the currency table) and a large parametrised test file. Version 0.5.1 (2026-03-19) added Egyptian pound, UAE dirham and Saudi riyal.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: BSD 3-Clause; pyproject declares BSD-3-Clause.
entries.popularity_note: about 352 GitHub stars; 14 open issues; PyPI about 1.35 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Pure Python, one dependency, no network use.
entries.verdict_reason: Small, permissive, tested, and already covers Gulf and Egyptian currencies.
entries.fit_in_engine: Normalising price strings captured from pages and feeds.

entries.name: metascraper
entries.claimed_description: Scrape metadata from any URL using Open Graph, JSON-LD, HTML meta tags, and smart fallbacks.
entries.actual_functionality: Monorepo of about 37 small packages (version 5.58.10, Node 22 or newer). Core plus rule packs for title, description, image, date and so on. The metascraper-amazon pack is 71 lines of CSS selectors for title, brand and main image on Amazon HTML that you supply; it does no fetching. No product-specific rules for price, GTIN, ratings or availability.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: MIT, copyright 2019 Microlink.
entries.popularity_note: about 2.8k GitHub stars; 9 open issues; npm metascraper 120,602 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: No install scripts in the core package. Parses untrusted HTML.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None (the vendor's Microlink API is optional).
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: None in itself; the Amazon rule pack only makes sense on pages obtained in a permitted way.
entries.verdict_reason: Good TypeScript-side framework for page metadata; we would add our own product rules (price, GTIN, rating) or do product extraction with extruct instead.
entries.fit_in_engine: SEO and metadata completeness checks on brand-site pages inside the Node application.

entries.name: Amazon SP-API SDK (official)
entries.claimed_description: The Selling Partner API SDK enables you to easily connect to and work with Amazon's REST-based SP-API.
entries.actual_functionality: About 17,000 generated files across five languages. The JavaScript package (@amazon-sp-api-release/amazon-sp-api-sdk-js) ships 64 API modules (A+ Content, Catalog Items, Listings Items, Customer Feedback, Data Kiosk, Reports and more) with TypeScript declarations and a built-in rate limiter (bottleneck). The README feature table shows the Python SDK has no rate limiter and that only Java and PHP support restricted-data tokens. The JavaScript package lists @babel/cli as a runtime dependency (unusual and heavy).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0, with NOTICE.
entries.popularity_note: about 103 GitHub stars; 33 open issues; release v1.15.0 on 2026-11-20; npm 20,760 downloads/week; PyPI amzn-sp-api 27,173 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Generated code from Amazon. Credentials are supplied by the caller. Caret/floor dependency ranges - lock them.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Amazon SP-API account, app registration and roles. Fees for third-party developers were announced for 2026; applicability to a private brand app not verified here.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: The official, compliant way to read and write our own catalogue, listing, A+ and report data.
entries.verdict_reason: First-party, permissive, current; use the JavaScript SDK in the Next.js app.
entries.fit_in_engine: Marketplace connector: listings, catalogue, A+ Content, customer feedback, reports, Data Kiosk.

entries.name: Amazon SP-API models (official)
entries.claimed_description: Swagger models for developers to use to create software that calls Selling Partner APIs.
entries.actual_functionality: 284 files: one model folder per API (57 folders including aplus-content, catalog-items, listings-items, product-type-definitions, customer-feedback, reports, data-kiosk), JSON schemas for feeds, notifications, reports and Data Kiosk (GraphQL), plus Java and C# auth helper libraries.
entries.language: JSON (OpenAPI), GraphQL; Java and C# helpers
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0, with NOTICE.
entries.popularity_note: about 936 GitHub stars; 262 open issues (the README sends API problems to Developer Support instead) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Data files only.
entries.verdict_reason: The source of truth for request and response shapes; generate TypeScript types and Zod validators from it.
entries.fit_in_engine: Type generation and validation of marketplace payloads; listing attribute schemas.

entries.name: amazon-sp-api (amz-tools, community Node client)
entries.claimed_description: Amazon Selling Partner API client: handles access tokens, calling the API, report download and rate limits.
entries.actual_functionality: About 196 files; plain JavaScript with TypeScript typings, a mocha test directory, sandbox mode, restore-rate handling and report helpers. Version 1.2.1 (2026-03-30). package.json now points its repository and homepage at a different GitHub account (jrl84/amazon-sp-api) and recent changelog entries link there. No CI workflows.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2020 amz-tools.
entries.popularity_note: about 265 GitHub stars; 35 open issues; npm amazon-sp-api 52,249 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Reads credentials from environment variables or a file in the home directory. Ownership appears to be moving between accounts - confirm who publishes the npm package before trusting updates.
entries.verdict_reason: Fine library, but the official SDK now exists and the maintainer transition adds supply-chain uncertainty.
entries.fit_in_engine: Fallback, or reference for report-download handling.

entries.name: python-amazon-sp-api (saleweaver, community Python client)
entries.claimed_description: A wrapper to access Amazon's Selling Partner API with an easy-to-use interface.
entries.actual_functionality: Version 2.1.44; 683 files: 53 API modules, documentation, tests. Supports credentials from environment, config file or AWS Secrets Manager.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2020 Michael Primke.
entries.popularity_note: about 693 GitHub stars; 0 open issues; PyPI 393,285 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Compatible-release pins. README carries sponsorship links. Nothing harmful seen.
entries.verdict_reason: Mature and permissive; a sensible choice for Python workers, where Amazon's own Python SDK lacks a rate limiter.
entries.fit_in_engine: Python batch workers pulling reports and catalogue data.

entries.name: ScaleLeap selling-partner-api-sdk
entries.claimed_description: A fully typed TypeScript and Node.js SDK library for Amazon Selling Partner API.
entries.actual_functionality: Generated TypeScript clients with tests and CI; version 8.4.0 dated 2025-01-26 is both the last release and the last commit. Pins axios 1.7.9.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2020 Scale Leap.
entries.popularity_note: about 74 GitHub stars; npm 2,068 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: 22 months without updates: API models and the pinned HTTP client are out of date.
entries.verdict_reason: Stale; superseded by Amazon's official SDK.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: PyABSA
entries.claimed_description: A modularized framework for reproducible aspect-based sentiment analysis: training, evaluation and inference across ABSA subtasks, with ready-to-use checkpoints.
entries.actual_functionality: Version 2.4.3; 586 files covering aspect term extraction, aspect polarity classification, triplet and quadruple extraction, with a "multilingual" checkpoint option. Checkpoints are fetched over HTTP at run time and their config and tokenizer files are loaded with pickle; one code path calls os.system to pip-install a package from a git URL and several others call it to download spaCy models; it also contains update-check and "emergency notification" routines that contact PyPI and the author's Hugging Face space. requirements.txt is unpinned and includes a git dependency.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2018 Yang Heng. The author's separate Hugging Face model yangheng/deberta-v3-base-absa-v1.1 is tagged MIT.
entries.popularity_note: about 1.1k GitHub stars; 68 open issues; PyPI 7,831 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: pickle.load on files downloaded at run time (code execution if the download source is ever tampered with); os.system calls that install software while the program runs; unpinned and git-based dependencies. Not suitable for a production worker as-is.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Downloads checkpoints from the author's hosting and Hugging Face.
entries.verdict_reason: Good research toolkit, unsafe runtime behaviour. Use the MIT-tagged DeBERTa ABSA model directly through transformers instead of the toolkit.
entries.fit_in_engine: Reference for aspect-based sentiment design; a candidate ABSA model for review mining (language coverage still to be checked).

entries.name: CAMeL Tools
entries.claimed_description: A suite of Arabic natural language processing tools developed by the CAMeL Lab at New York University Abu Dhabi.
entries.actual_functionality: Version 1.6.0 (Python 3.11 or newer); 138 files with tests. Modules for pre-processing, morphology, disambiguation, tagging, dialect identification, named entities and sentiment. Models and databases are downloaded separately with the camel_data tool from a published catalogue. In catalogue 1.6 the sentiment packages are licensed "AraBERT" (custom) and "Apache 2.0" (mBERT version); other packages are MIT, GPL v2, CC BY 4.0 or LDC.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2018-2026 New York University Abu Dhabi. Data packages carry their own licences - choose the Apache-2.0 mBERT sentiment pack, or the CAMeL-Lab sentiment models on Hugging Face (tagged apache-2.0); avoid the AraBERT-, GPL- and LDC-licensed packs unless cleared.
entries.popularity_note: about 594 GitHub stars; 29 open issues; PyPI 40,068 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Downloads and unzips data packages from GitHub releases; uses dill (pickle-style) serialisation for some models. Pin the catalogue version and mirror the packages internally.
entries.verdict_reason: The strongest permissively licensed Arabic toolkit found; restrict it to the permissively licensed data packs.
entries.fit_in_engine: Arabic review pre-processing, dialect detection and sentiment in the Python review-mining worker.

entries.name: AraBERT
entries.claimed_description: Code and implementation for AraBERT v2, AraGPT2 and AraELECTRA.
entries.actual_functionality: 104 files: pre-processing code, training scripts and example notebooks for Arabic language models published by the American University of Beirut. No root licence file; each model folder has its own custom "Software License Agreement".
entries.licence_note: Custom licence in arabert/LICENSE: free use for any purpose, but "If you remix, transform, or build upon the material, you must distribute your contributions under the same license" and you must also abide by the licences of the tools it builds on (it names the Farasa segmenter). The aubmindlab models on Hugging Face declare no licence tag. Needs legal review before any use.
entries.popularity_note: about 738 GitHub stars; PyPI arabert 1,455 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Old, unpinned dependencies.
entries.verdict_reason: Non-standard licence with share-alike and third-party conditions, and no maintenance for four years.
entries.fit_in_engine: None (use CAMeLBERT models instead).

entries.name: SetFit
entries.claimed_description: An efficient and prompt-free framework for few-shot fine-tuning of Sentence Transformers; high accuracy with little labelled data.
entries.actual_functionality: 192 files; repository version 1.3.0.dev0, latest release 1.2.0. Includes a span module for aspect-based sentiment: an aspect extractor built on a spaCy pipeline plus two SetFit classifiers (aspect filter and polarity). Aspect coverage therefore depends on the spaCy language model chosen (Arabic support not verified).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0. Base embedding models have their own licences (for example BAAI/bge-m3 and intfloat/multilingual-e5-small are tagged MIT on Hugging Face).
entries.popularity_note: about 2.9k GitHub stars; 150 open issues; PyPI 134,668 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: trust_remote_code defaults to False (verified). Downloads models from Hugging Face - pin model revisions.
entries.verdict_reason: Permissive and maintained; lets us train category-specific aspect and sentiment classifiers from a small labelled set of our own reviews.
entries.fit_in_engine: Custom aspect and sentiment classifiers for beauty/personal-care review themes (Python worker).

entries.name: XLM-T (multilingual Twitter sentiment)
entries.claimed_description: Data, code and pre-trained multilingual language models for Twitter.
entries.actual_functionality: 66 files: notebooks, evaluation script and tweet sentiment datasets for eight languages (Arabic, English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese). The models live on Hugging Face (cardiffnlp/twitter-xlm-roberta-base-sentiment: 279,861 downloads, last modified 2023-07-19). Trained on tweets, not product reviews.
entries.licence_note: Repository LICENSE: Apache-2.0. The Hugging Face cards for cardiffnlp/twitter-xlm-roberta-base-sentiment and its "-multilingual" variant carry no licence tag (checked via the Hugging Face API on 2026-11-26), and the bundled tweet datasets have their own terms. Model licence is therefore unclear.
entries.popularity_note: about 167 GitHub stars; 8 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Notebook code only.
entries.verdict_reason: Useful benchmark, but unclear model licence, tweet-domain training and no maintenance. Prefer models with explicit licences (for example lxyuan/distilbert-base-multilingual-cased-sentiments-student, tagged apache-2.0 and listing Arabic).
entries.fit_in_engine: Baseline for evaluating multilingual review sentiment.

entries.name: sharp
entries.claimed_description: High performance Node.js image processing, the fastest module to resize JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF and TIFF images.
entries.actual_functionality: Version 0.35.5 (Node 20.9 or newer); 804 files with an extensive test suite. Native add-on with prebuilt binaries delivered as optional per-platform packages. Exposes dimensions, format, colour space, per-channel statistics, trimming and compositing - enough for resolution, aspect-ratio and white-background checks.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0. The prebuilt libvips binary packages are LGPL-3.0-or-later (npm registry metadata) - acceptable when used unmodified as a library.
entries.popularity_note: about 33k GitHub stars; 120 open issues; npm about 166 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Installs prebuilt native binaries. Decoding untrusted images is a classic attack surface - keep it patched and cap input size.
entries.verdict_reason: De-facto standard, permissive, very active, native to our stack.
entries.fit_in_engine: Hero-image technical checks: pixel dimensions, aspect ratio, file format, background whiteness, product fill ratio.

entries.name: IQA-PyTorch (pyiqa)
entries.claimed_description: An Image Quality Assessment toolbox with pure python and pytorch.
entries.actual_functionality: 249 files implementing many full-reference and no-reference quality metrics with downloadable weights. Version 0.1.16 on PyPI.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0; a second file, LICENSE-S-Lab (NTU S-Lab License), also restricts use to non-commercial purposes. PyPI metadata says the same. A business may not use it without a separate commercial licence.
entries.popularity_note: about 3.5k GitHub stars; 54 open issues; PyPI 142,052 downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Downloads model weights at run time.
entries.verdict_reason: Non-commercial licence - not usable in a business application.
entries.fit_in_engine: None (use sharp/OpenCV measures or commission a licensed model).

entries.name: rembg
entries.claimed_description: Rembg is a tool to remove image backgrounds ("Fast and accurate background remover API").
entries.actual_functionality: 135 files; version 2.0.88. Python library, CLI and HTTP server wrapping about 20 segmentation models run with ONNX Runtime; models download on first use from the project's GitHub releases with checksum verification. The default model in code and CLI is "bria-rmbg" (BRIA RMBG-2.0). Also offers two cloud back ends (withoutBG, Atlas Cloud); the README promotes withoutBG with referral links.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.txt: MIT for the code. Models have their own licences: briaai/RMBG-2.0 is gated with licence "other" on Hugging Face and BRIA's RMBG-1.4 card says "source-available ... for non-commercial use"; ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet is tagged MIT. Set the model explicitly (for example birefnet-general) and confirm the licence of whichever model is used.
entries.popularity_note: about 26k GitHub stars; 0 open issues; PyPI about 5.1 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: The bundled server binds to 0.0.0.0 by default. The cloud back ends send images to third parties if selected. Model files are fetched at run time - mirror them internally.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None for local models; optional paid cloud APIs.
entries.verdict_reason: Useful and permissive code, but only with an explicitly chosen, commercially usable model and the cloud back ends disabled.
entries.fit_in_engine: Foreground mask for hero-image checks (product fill percentage, background purity, cropping).

entries.name: OpenCV
entries.claimed_description: OpenCV: Open Source Computer Vision Library.
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (7,444 files; licence, version header and layout only). Development version 5.2.0-dev; latest release 5.1.0. Bundles third-party libraries (FFmpeg wrappers, libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp, protobuf and others) with their own licences.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0 for OpenCV itself; bundled third-party components keep their own licences. Use opencv-python-headless on servers.
entries.popularity_note: about 92k GitHub stars; 2.6k open issues; PyPI opencv-python-headless about 68.8 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Large native code base that parses many image formats - keep it current and decode untrusted images in an isolated worker.
entries.verdict_reason: Permissive, ubiquitous, and sufficient for rule-based image checks.
entries.fit_in_engine: Blur (Laplacian variance), border/background uniformity, text-overlay and bounding-box checks in the Python image worker.

entries.name: idealo image-quality-assessment (NIMA)
entries.claimed_description: An implementation of an aesthetic and technical image quality model based on Google's research paper "NIMA: Neural Image Assessment".
entries.actual_functionality: 95 files: training and prediction code for Python 3.6 / Keras, Docker files, and two MobileNet weight files (aesthetic, trained on AVA; technical, trained on TID2013) committed in the repository.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0 for the code. The weights were trained on the AVA and TID2013 research datasets, whose terms were not checked.
entries.popularity_note: about 2.2k GitHub stars; 36 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Pins pillow 5.0.x and targets Python 3.6, both long out of support; binary weight files are committed in the repository.
entries.verdict_reason: Unmaintained since 2019 and built on obsolete dependencies.
entries.fit_in_engine: None (concept reference only: learned aesthetic score).

entries.name: IMG.LY background-removal-js
entries.claimed_description: Background Removal in the Browser and Node.js.
entries.actual_functionality: 134 files; workspace version 1.7.0 (npm latest 1.4.5 for the Node package). Runs an ONNX segmentation model in the browser or Node.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md is the AGPL text and the README says "free for use under the AGPL License", with other licensing by contacting the vendor.
entries.popularity_note: about 7.4k GitHub stars; 16 open issues; npm @imgly/background-removal-node 72,050 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Pins old onnxruntime-node (1.21.0) and sharp (0.32).
entries.verdict_reason: AGPL network copyleft inside our own application code; a permissive alternative exists (rembg with a permissive model).
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: Docling
entries.claimed_description: Docling simplifies document processing by parsing diverse formats - including advanced PDF understanding - and providing seamless integrations with the generative AI ecosystem.
entries.actual_functionality: Version 2.153.0 (released the day before inspection); 2,039 files with a large test suite and CI. Modular Python packages for PDF (layout and table models), DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, Markdown, e-mail, audio and more; several OCR engines as optional extras; chunking for retrieval. Models are downloaded with a docling-tools command and can be pre-fetched for offline use. README: "Local execution capabilities for sensitive data and air-gapped environments".
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT ("The Docling Contributors"). README: "For individual model usage, please refer to the model licenses found in the original packages" - check each model and OCR engine used.
entries.popularity_note: about 71k GitHub stars; 778 open issues; PyPI about 4.4 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Parses untrusted documents and downloads models when first used - pre-fetch them with the docling-tools command, pin versions and run in an isolated worker. Very fast release cadence means frequent upgrades.
entries.verdict_reason: Best open option for complex PDFs (brand guidelines, retailer style guides with tables); permissive and very active.
entries.fit_in_engine: Knowledge-base ingestion worker for PDFs and Office files that need layout and table fidelity.

entries.name: Unstructured
entries.claimed_description: Open-source pre-processing tools for unstructured data: "a library that prepares raw documents for downstream ML tasks".
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (1,362 files; licence, manifest, README and telemetry code). Version 0.27.38; Python 3.11-3.13. Partitions PDF, Office, HTML, e-mail and images into typed elements. Heavy dependency set (spaCy, numba, lxml, python-magic). Depends on unstructured-client, the client for the vendor's hosted API.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: Apache-2.0.
entries.popularity_note: about 16k GitHub stars; 190 open issues; PyPI about 2.6 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: README: the library "sends lightweight analytics" to packages.unstructured.io by default - one ping when imported and one per top-level partition call; opt out by setting DO_NOT_TRACK or SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS before import. Large native dependency surface.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None required; the vendor also offers a hosted API (commercial, not assessed).
entries.verdict_reason: Capable and permissive, but heavier than Docling/MarkItDown and it phones home by default - only add it if a format gap appears, with telemetry disabled.
entries.fit_in_engine: Fallback parser for unusual formats in the knowledge-base pipeline.

entries.name: MarkItDown
entries.claimed_description: A lightweight Python utility for converting various files to Markdown for use with LLMs and related text analysis pipelines.
entries.actual_functionality: Version 0.1.9 (Python 3.10 or newer). Four packages: markitdown (core, with a tests folder of 23 files), markitdown-mcp (an MCP server), markitdown-ocr and a sample plugin. Converters are optional extras (pptx, docx, xlsx, xls, pdf, Outlook, audio transcription, YouTube transcripts, Azure Document Intelligence). Plugins are disabled by default.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT (Microsoft Corporation).
entries.popularity_note: about 199k GitHub stars; 323 open issues; PyPI about 20 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: README warning: it "performs I/O with the privileges of the current process" - it will read any local path or URL it is handed, so validate inputs and call the narrowest convert function. Optional features send content to external services (Azure, LLM image description) only if configured.
entries.verdict_reason: Simple, permissive and good enough for most brand documents; pair with Docling for hard PDFs.
entries.fit_in_engine: Default converter for Word/PowerPoint/Excel/HTML brand documents entering the knowledge base.

entries.name: unpdf
entries.claimed_description: Utilities for PDF extraction and rendering across all JavaScript runtimes - especially useful for AI applications that need to summarize or analyze PDF documents.
entries.actual_functionality: 73 files; version 2.2.3 released on the day of inspection; no runtime dependencies (ships a serverless build of PDF.js; optional peer @napi-rs/canvas for rendering pages to images). Functions such as extractText, getMeta, extractImages and renderPageAsImage; tests and CI. README says Node.js 24 or newer.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT (Johann Schopplich). The bundled PDF.js is Apache-2.0 (npm metadata for pdfjs-dist).
entries.popularity_note: about 1.3k GitHub stars; 0 open issues; npm about 12.9 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Parses untrusted PDFs with PDF.js inside the Node process - keep it updated and limit file size and time.
entries.verdict_reason: Native to the TypeScript stack, tiny, permissive.
entries.fit_in_engine: Quick text extraction from PDFs inside the Next.js app or Node workers (simple documents, retailer spec sheets).

entries.name: mammoth.js
entries.claimed_description: Convert Word documents from docx to simple HTML and Markdown, using the semantic information in the document.
entries.actual_functionality: 124 files; version 1.13.0; test suite and CI. Style mapping from Word styles to HTML; images handled through converters; access to external files referenced by a document is disabled by default.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: BSD 2-Clause (Michael Williamson).
entries.popularity_note: about 6.3k GitHub stars; 58 open issues; npm about 16.6 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: README: "Mammoth performs no sanitisation of the source document, and should therefore be used extremely carefully with untrusted user input" - sanitise the HTML it produces before storing or displaying it.
entries.verdict_reason: Stable, permissive, does one job well.
entries.fit_in_engine: Converting Word-based brand guidelines and briefs in the Node application (sanitise output).

entries.name: pgvector
entries.claimed_description: Open-source vector similarity search for Postgres.
entries.actual_functionality: 161 files of C with regression tests. Extension version 0.8.7 (0.9.0 in preparation). Vector, half-precision, sparse and bit vector types; HNSW and IVFFlat indexes; L2, inner-product and cosine distance.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: the PostgreSQL License (a permissive BSD/MIT-style licence).
entries.popularity_note: about 24k GitHub stars; 12 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Runs inside the database server - install only from a trusted package or managed-database provider and track releases.
entries.verdict_reason: Keeps embeddings in the PostgreSQL we already run; permissive and mature.
entries.fit_in_engine: Knowledge-base retrieval, similar-product and duplicate-content search, review-theme clustering.

entries.name: pgvector-node
entries.claimed_description: pgvector support for Node.js, Deno, and Bun (and TypeScript).
entries.actual_functionality: 87 files; version 0.3.1 (2026-11-04); no runtime dependencies; tests against many ORMs and drivers; Node 22 or newer.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.txt: MIT (Andrew Kane).
entries.popularity_note: about 445 GitHub stars; 1 open issue; npm about 1.1 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: No dependencies, no install scripts.
entries.verdict_reason: Official companion to pgvector for our Node stack.
entries.fit_in_engine: Database access layer for embeddings.

entries.name: Transformers.js
entries.claimed_description: Run Transformers directly in your browser (or Node.js), with no need for a server.
entries.actual_functionality: 762 files; package @huggingface/transformers version 4.3.2. Pipeline tasks found in source include feature-extraction (embeddings), text-classification (sentiment), zero-shot-classification, image-classification, zero-shot-image-classification, image-segmentation and background-removal. Models are fetched from huggingface.co by default (allowRemoteModels is true and the remote host is the Hugging Face Hub - verified in env.js); local-only loading is supported.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0. Each model has its own licence: intfloat/multilingual-e5-small and BAAI/bge-m3 are tagged MIT; Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 apache-2.0; Xenova/multilingual-e5-small has no licence tag (Hugging Face API, 2026-11-26).
entries.popularity_note: about 16k GitHub stars; 241 open issues; npm about 4.5 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Pulls a native ONNX Runtime binary and, by default, model files from the internet at run time. Set allowRemoteModels to false, ship vetted model files with the app and pin revisions.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None (Hugging Face Hub only for model download).
entries.verdict_reason: Lets the TypeScript app create multilingual embeddings locally at no per-call cost; permissive.
entries.fit_in_engine: Embedding generation for the knowledge base and semantic matching; lightweight sentiment or zero-shot image classification in Node.

entries.name: gtin (xbpf)
entries.claimed_description: GTIN (UPC, EAN, ITF, etc.) utilities.
entries.actual_functionality: Three source files (190 lines) with jest tests: isGTIN (format), isValid (check digit), getFormat, minify, getRealFormat and UPC-E expand/compress. Version 1.0.2.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2020 Ivan K.
entries.popularity_note: about 19 GitHub stars; npm gtin 41,964 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: No dependencies. Throws on non-string or malformed input - wrap calls.
entries.verdict_reason: The algorithm is fixed by GS1, so staleness matters little; copy the logic (with attribution) into our validation module with our own tests rather than depend on an unmaintained package.
entries.fit_in_engine: GTIN/EAN/UPC check-digit validation in listing data quality rules.

entries.name: barcode-core
entries.claimed_description: Zero-dependency UPC / EAN / ISBN / ITF-14 check-digit math, validation, UPC-E expansion, and random/sequential code generation.
entries.actual_functionality: Six source files (about 260 lines) and one test file; version 0.2.0. Besides validation it generates random and sequential codes; described as the engine behind a barcode-generator website.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2026 upcgen.com.
entries.popularity_note: 0 GitHub stars; the package name returned "not found" from the npm registry on 2026-11-26 (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: No dependencies. Code generation is irrelevant to us and inappropriate for a brand owner (GTINs must come from GS1 allocations).
entries.verdict_reason: Unadopted and unpublished; nothing here that 20 lines of our own code would not do.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: python-stdnum
entries.claimed_description: A Python module to parse, validate and reformat standard numbers and codes.
entries.actual_functionality: 816 files; version 2.2. The ean module validates EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC (12-digit) and GTIN-14 check digits; gs1_128 parses GS1 application identifiers; isbn is included. Doctest-based test suite.
entries.licence_note: COPYING: GNU LGPL; source headers say version 2.1 "or (at your option) any later version". Weak copyleft: using it unmodified as an installed library places no obligation on our own code.
entries.popularity_note: about 611 GitHub stars; 91 open issues; PyPI about 8.1 million downloads/month (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Pure Python, no required dependencies, no network use for EAN checks.
entries.verdict_reason: Trusted and widely used; fine under LGPL when installed unmodified from PyPI.
entries.fit_in_engine: GTIN and GS1 validation in Python data-quality workers.

entries.name: json-rules-engine
entries.claimed_description: A rules engine expressed in JSON.
entries.actual_functionality: About 1,470 lines of source, 31 test files, TypeScript typings; repository version 7.3.2 (npm 7.3.1). Rules are plain JSON with nested ALL/ANY conditions, custom operators, facts resolved asynchronously, priorities and caching. No eval or dynamic code execution found in src.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: ISC (permissive, equivalent in effect to MIT), copyright 2017 Cache Hamm.
entries.popularity_note: about 3.2k GitHub stars; 61 open issues; npm 497,953 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Uses jsonpath-plus to read facts - keep that dependency current and never let untrusted users author rule paths.
entries.verdict_reason: Rules stored as JSON rows in PostgreSQL can be edited without code releases; small and permissive.
entries.fit_in_engine: Content-rule engine: retailer-specific title/bullet/image requirements expressed as data.

entries.name: Zod
entries.claimed_description: TypeScript-first schema validation with static type inference.
entries.actual_functionality: 746 files; version 4.6.7; no runtime dependencies; extensive tests and CI.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2025 Colin McDonnell.
entries.popularity_note: about 44k GitHub stars; 115 open issues; npm about 463 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: No dependencies, no install scripts.
entries.verdict_reason: Already the default in the Next.js/TypeScript ecosystem; also used by most MCP servers inspected.
entries.fit_in_engine: Validating API payloads, LLM structured outputs and listing data shapes.

entries.name: GoRules ZEN Engine
entries.claimed_description: A cross-platform, open-source Business Rules Engine written in Rust, with native bindings for Node.js, Python, Go and others; decisions are stored as portable JSON.
entries.actual_functionality: 805 files: Rust core, bindings for Node.js, Python, C and mobile, benchmarks and test data; Node package @gorules/zen-engine 2.1.12 delivered as prebuilt native binaries. Decision tables, expression language, switch and function nodes. The visual editor is a separate repository (not inspected).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2023 GoRules.io.
entries.popularity_note: about 2.2k GitHub stars; 35 open issues; npm 155,385 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Native binary dependency; function nodes execute rule-author-supplied code, so rule authorship must be restricted.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None (the vendor also offers hosted tooling, not assessed).
entries.verdict_reason: More power than needed at the start; revisit if business users must edit decision tables visually.
entries.fit_in_engine: Possible later upgrade of the content-rules engine.

entries.name: n8n
entries.claimed_description: Fair-code platform to build and deploy AI agents and workflows, with 1500+ integrations; self-hosted or cloud.
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (36,777 files; licences, manifests, README, file listing). Version 2.50.0 in the repository (npm 2.49.7); Node 24 or newer. 1,317 files sit under ".ee" paths, which are covered by the separate n8n Enterprise License. Built-in nodes include Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento and AWS; no Amazon selling-partner node was found by directory name.
key_dependencies: PostgreSQL or SQLite (pg and sqlite3 drivers)
about 173 direct dependencies in the CLI package
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: Sustainable Use License 1.0 - "You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or personal use"; distribution only free of charge for non-commercial purposes. Files with ".ee" in their name or folder need a paid n8n Enterprise License for production (LICENSE_EE.md). So: internal use is allowed, but it is source-available, not open source, and it could not be part of anything offered to other companies.
entries.popularity_note: about 212k GitHub stars; 308 open issues; npm 106,555 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Large dependency surface; a workflow tool holds credentials for every connected system and executes user-written code nodes - treat as high-privilege infrastructure. Enterprise-licensed areas, judging by folder names, include the AI workflow builder, source control, external secrets, log streaming and environments.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Self-hosting is free under the licence; n8n Cloud and Enterprise are paid.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: A web-search result showed a community n8n template that pairs it with a scraping service to monitor competitor prices; the same marketplace-terms limits apply to anything built this way.
entries.verdict_reason: Licence restricts use to internal purposes and mixes in enterprise-licensed code; a permissively licensed job queue (pg-boss) covers our scheduling needs without that constraint.
entries.fit_in_engine: None as a platform component. Could only be a stand-alone internal back-office tool, after legal sign-off.

entries.name: Activepieces
entries.claimed_description: All-in-one AI automation designed to be extensible through a type-safe pieces framework written in TypeScript; pieces are also available as MCP servers.
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (37,189 files; licences, manifest, README, file listing). Version 0.95.0 in the repository (latest release 0.94.0). 232 files sit in the enterprise directories. Community pieces include Shopify, WooCommerce and several AWS services; no Amazon selling-partner piece was found by directory name.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT ("MIT Expat") for everything except packages/ee/ and packages/server/api/src/app/ee, which fall under the Activepieces Enterprise licence (production use requires a paid subscription). A self-hosted deployment must not enable the enterprise code.
entries.popularity_note: about 26k GitHub stars; 496 open issues; release v0.94.0 the day before inspection (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Same class of risk as any automation hub: stores third-party credentials and runs code steps. Pre-1.0 version numbers and a very fast release cadence.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Self-hosted community edition is free; cloud and enterprise editions are paid.
entries.verdict_reason: If a no-code automation canvas is ever wanted, this is the permissively licensed choice - deploy the MIT core only. Not needed for the first release.
entries.fit_in_engine: Optional later: business-user automations (alerts, report distribution) around the engine.

entries.name: Windmill
entries.claimed_description: Open-source, self-hostable code-first platform for workflows, apps and AI agents.
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (11,700 files; licence files, README). Rust back end with a web IDE; scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, Bash and others become jobs, flows and UIs; PostgreSQL-backed. Release v1.885.0.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: files are AGPLv3 unless stated; client libraries and OpenAPI files are Apache-2.0; code behind the "enterprise" flag is proprietary. The official "Community Edition" images also contain proprietary code, free to use within built-in limits but not to "sell, resell, serve as a managed service, modify or wrap"; exposing Windmill to your own users as a product feature needs a commercial licence.
entries.popularity_note: about 19k GitHub stars; 574 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Executes arbitrary scripts by design - needs strong isolation and access control.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Self-hosting is free within the licence terms; the vendor sells commercial licences and hosted plans (pricing not checked).
entries.verdict_reason: AGPL plus proprietary carve-outs is too much licence complexity for a job runner.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: Trigger.dev
entries.claimed_description: The open-source platform for building AI workflows in TypeScript: long-running tasks with retries, queues, LLM observability, and elastic scaling.
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (8,584 files; licences, manifests, README, self-hosting compose file). SDK @trigger.dev/sdk 4.8.10. The Docker self-hosting stack defines the web app plus PostgreSQL, Redis, ElectricSQL, ClickHouse, a container registry, MinIO object storage and a stream store.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0; the published SDK package declares MIT. Both permissive.
entries.popularity_note: about 17k GitHub stars; 204 open issues; npm @trigger.dev/sdk about 1.7 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Self-hosting means operating and patching seven-plus services. The cloud option sends job payloads to a third party.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Trigger.dev Cloud is a commercial hosted service (pricing not checked); self-hosting is free but operationally heavy.
entries.verdict_reason: Good permissive option if we outgrow a simple queue and need long-running, observable AI workflows; too much infrastructure for day one.
entries.fit_in_engine: Later: orchestration of long multi-step audits (crawl, extract, score, report).

entries.name: Inngest
entries.claimed_description: Durable functions that replace queues, state management, and scheduling, so developers can write reliable step functions without touching infrastructure.
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (16,405 files; licence, README). Go server and CLI, release v1.53.0; the TypeScript SDK lives in a separate repository (not inspected).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: Server Side Public License v1 with a "Grant of Future License" clause: Apache-2.0 becomes available "on the third anniversary of the date we make the Software available". README: SDKs are Apache-2.0. SSPL is not an OSI-approved open-source licence.
entries.popularity_note: about 6.1k GitHub stars; 49 open issues; npm inngest about 3.5 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Not assessed beyond licence.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Inngest Cloud is a commercial hosted service (pricing not checked); self-hosting falls under SSPL.
entries.verdict_reason: SSPL server; pg-boss or Trigger.dev do the job under permissive licences.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: pg-boss
entries.claimed_description: Queueing jobs in Postgres from Node.js like a boss.
entries.actual_functionality: 434 files; version 12.40.0 released the day before inspection; Node 22.12 or newer. Uses PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED for reliable delivery; cron scheduling, retries, dead-letter queues; test suite and CI; optional dashboard and proxy packages in the same repository.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2016 Tim Jones.
entries.popularity_note: about 4.2k GitHub stars; 8 open issues; npm about 5.1 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Four dependencies; creates its own schema in the database (grant it a dedicated role).
entries.verdict_reason: Fits "TypeScript on PostgreSQL" exactly: scheduled crawls, API pulls and report jobs without adding Redis.
entries.fit_in_engine: Job scheduling and background processing for the whole engine.

entries.name: BullMQ
entries.claimed_description: The fastest, most reliable, Redis-based distributed queue for Node.js, Python, Elixir, .NET, Rust, PHP, and more.
entries.actual_functionality: 1,266 files; version 6.7.10; exact-pinned dependencies; CodeQL and OSV-scanner workflows; tests in several languages. Delayed and repeatable jobs, rate limiting, flows (parent/child jobs).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2018 BullForce Labs AB and contributors.
entries.popularity_note: about 9.6k GitHub stars; 296 open issues; npm about 13.7 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Adds Redis as a second stateful system to secure and back up. The vendor sells a "Pro" edition (not in this repo).
entries.verdict_reason: Excellent and permissive - choose it only if job volume outgrows pg-boss, since it brings Redis with it.
entries.fit_in_engine: Alternative job queue at higher throughput.

entries.name: ExcelJS
entries.claimed_description: Excel Workbook Manager - read and write xlsx and csv files.
entries.actual_functionality: 546 files; version 4.4.0 with unit and integration tests. Styles, formulas, images, data validation, streaming writers. Dependencies are held at old major versions (archiver 5, unzipper 0.10, uuid 8, saxes 5).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2014-2019 Guyon Roche.
entries.popularity_note: about 16k GitHub stars; 671 open issues; npm about 29 million downloads/week; last release v4.4.0 (October 2023) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Unmaintained for almost three years with ageing transitive dependencies - run a dependency audit, use it only to write files we generate (do not parse untrusted uploads with it) and hide it behind our own interface so it can be swapped.
entries.verdict_reason: Still the practical choice for formatted Excel reports in Node, but treat it as frozen software: pin it, wrap it, and plan a replacement.
entries.fit_in_engine: Excel exports of audits and scorecards.

entries.name: PDFKit
entries.claimed_description: A JavaScript PDF generation library for Node and the browser.
entries.actual_functionality: 412 files; version 0.21.0 (2026-11-19) with tests and CI. Low-level drawing API; font embedding through fontkit.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2014 Devon Govett.
entries.popularity_note: about 11k GitHub stars; 265 open issues; npm about 19 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Few dependencies; no install scripts beyond build-on-publish.
entries.verdict_reason: Stable, permissive foundation; it is also what react-pdf renders with.
entries.fit_in_engine: Server-side PDF report generation.

entries.name: react-pdf
entries.claimed_description: React renderer for PDFs: a package "used to create PDFs using React".
entries.actual_functionality: 1,572 files; @react-pdf/renderer 4.9.2, built on PDFKit 0.21.0; supports React 16.8 to 19; layout engine with flexbox-style rules; active release workflow.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2017-present Diego Muracciole.
entries.popularity_note: about 17k GitHub stars; 288 open issues; npm @react-pdf/renderer about 10 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Nothing notable; fonts and images are fetched from whatever URLs our templates reference.
entries.verdict_reason: Matches a React/Next.js team's skills; permissive and active.
entries.fit_in_engine: Branded PDF scorecards and audit reports.

entries.name: pdf-lib
entries.claimed_description: Create and modify PDF documents in any JavaScript environment.
entries.actual_functionality: 759 files; version 1.17.1 is both the last release and the last commit (2021-11-11). The pdfme project maintains its own fork of it.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: MIT, copyright 2019 Andrew Dillon.
entries.popularity_note: about 8.7k GitHub stars; 279 open issues; npm about 34 million downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Five years without fixes while still parsing complex PDF input.
entries.verdict_reason: Unmaintained; for new work use PDFKit/react-pdf, or a maintained fork if existing PDFs must be modified.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: pdfme
entries.claimed_description: TypeScript-based PDF generator and React-based UI. Open source and free to use under the MIT license.
entries.actual_functionality: 1,413 files; packages for generator, designer UI, schemas, converter, manipulator, CLI and its own maintained pdf-lib fork; release v6.2.8. Templates are JSON, so non-developers can adjust report layouts in the designer.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: MIT, copyright 2020 HandDot.
entries.popularity_note: about 5.1k GitHub stars; 40 open issues; npm @pdfme/generator 317,834 downloads/week (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Peer dependencies are declared as "latest" between its own packages - pin exact versions in our lock file.
entries.verdict_reason: Safe to adopt if business users need to edit report templates themselves; otherwise react-pdf is enough.
entries.fit_in_engine: Optional: user-editable PDF report templates.

entries.name: Akeneo PIM Community Edition
entries.claimed_description: Akeneo PIM development repository ("Welcome to Akeneo PIM Product").
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (16,025 files; licence, composer manifest, README, compose file). Version 2026.5; PHP 8.3, Symfony, Doctrine; the development compose file uses MySQL 8.4 and Elasticsearch 8.17. The README directs new projects to the separate pim-community-standard repository (not inspected).
entries.licence_note: LICENCE.txt: Open Software License 3.0 - a copyleft licence that also treats making the software available over a network as distribution, so modified versions offered to outside users must be shared under the same licence. Running it unmodified for internal staff is permitted.
entries.popularity_note: about 1.1k GitHub stars; 371 open issues; release v2026.5 (October 2026) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Large PHP application with its own patch cycle; not assessed in depth.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None for the community edition; the vendor's commercial editions were not assessed.
entries.verdict_reason: A second technology stack (PHP, MySQL, Elasticsearch) and a copyleft licence; valuable mainly as a reference data model for attributes, families, channels and completeness.
entries.fit_in_engine: Data-model reference for our product content schema; integrate by API only if the business already runs Akeneo.

entries.name: Pimcore
entries.claimed_description: Open Core Platform for Product Experience Management: "One platform. Any data. Any channel. Any process."
entries.actual_functionality: Read selectively (3,200 files; licence, composer manifest, README). PHP 8.4/8.5 on Symfony and Doctrine; release v2026.3.7. composer.json declares the licence as "proprietary".
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.md: Pimcore Open Core License (last updated June 2025). Free production use only for organisations with total global revenue up to EUR 5 million that are not part of a larger group, and for non-profit/educational bodies; Pimcore decides eligibility "at its own reasonable discretion" and may audit. Hosting it for third parties or building a competing product is prohibited. AtroPIM's README dates the switch to this licence to "Platform Version 2025.1"; earlier versions and their terms were not inspected.
entries.popularity_note: about 3.9k GitHub stars; 104 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Not assessed beyond licence.
entries.external_api_dependencies: A paid Pimcore licence would be needed if the brand owner's group revenue is above the threshold.
entries.verdict_reason: Source-available with a revenue threshold a brand owner will exceed; using it without a paid licence would breach its terms.
entries.fit_in_engine: None unless the business buys Pimcore.

entries.name: UnoPim
entries.claimed_description: An open-source Product Information Management (PIM) and Digital Asset Management (DAM) platform built on Laravel 13.
entries.actual_functionality: 4,631 files; release v3.1.4; PHP 8.4 and Laravel 13. Modules include Product, Attribute, Category, Completeness, DataTransfer (import/export), HistoryControl, AdminApi (REST with OAuth), Webhook, MagicAI and AiAgent, ProductPassport, Measurement. Runs on MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL 16; Elasticsearch optional. Tests: Pest feature tests, Playwright end-to-end tests, and CI jobs for each database. Published by Webkul.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: MIT, copyright 2010-2026 Webkul Software.
entries.popularity_note: about 11k GitHub stars; 19 open issues; release v3.1.4 in the week of inspection (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: A separate PHP application to patch and secure; AI features call whichever LLM provider is configured. composer currently requires the MySQL PHP extension even on PostgreSQL hosts (README note).
entries.external_api_dependencies: None required; optional LLM provider keys for the AI features.
entries.verdict_reason: The only permissively licensed, actively developed PIM found. Adopt only if the business needs a PIM back office - run it as a separate service and integrate through its API rather than merging code.
entries.fit_in_engine: Optional system of record for product content feeding the engine; reference for completeness scoring.

entries.name: AtroPIM
entries.claimed_description: AtroPIM lets manufacturers, wholesalers, and distributors consolidate product information in one system and distribute it to shops, marketplaces, catalogues and ERP systems.
entries.actual_functionality: 518 files: the PIM module only (products, variants, classifications, channels, catalogues); it requires the AtroCore platform ^3.0 (separate repository, not inspected). Release v1.17.0. No test directory in this repository. Its README compares itself with Akeneo and Pimcore and notes Pimcore's licence change.
key_dependencies: MySQL or PostgreSQL (per vendor documentation, not verified)
entries.licence_note: LICENSE.txt: GNU GPL v3; composer.json says GPL-3.0-only. Strong copyleft: fine to run internally, but any modified version we distribute must be GPL too. Keep it a separate service; do not copy its code into ours.
entries.popularity_note: about 213 GitHub stars; 1 open issue (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Not assessed in depth; depends on a platform that was not inspected.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None for the open-source core; the vendor's commercial offerings were not assessed.
entries.verdict_reason: Viable as an unmodified stand-alone service, but GPL, a second stack and small community make UnoPim the better first look.
entries.fit_in_engine: Alternative PIM candidate; data-model reference.

entries.name: changedetection.io
entries.claimed_description: Monitor websites for updates and get notified - ideal for monitoring price changes, content edits, conditional changes and LLM change summaries.
entries.actual_functionality: 1,344 files; version 0.70.4; Flask application with tests. Fetchers: plain HTTP, Playwright and Selenium. A "restock and price" processor reads schema.org metadata with extruct and price-parser; conditional triggers, per-watch proxies, optional LLM summaries through LiteLLM, many notification channels.
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: Apache-2.0. NOTICE: the name, logo and brand assets are not licensed.
entries.popularity_note: about 36k GitHub stars; 328 open issues; PyPI 20,673 downloads/month (the README's main install route is Docker) (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: A fetch-anything service: keep it on an internal network with outbound allow-listing. The README recommends a commercial proxy network through a referral link and promotes the author's hosted plan.
entries.external_api_dependencies: None for self-hosting; hosted plan advertised at $8.99/month; optional proxies and LLM keys.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Tool is neutral. Monitoring our own brand site and consenting retailers is fine; pointing it (especially with proxies) at marketplaces that prohibit automated access is not.
entries.verdict_reason: The most credible open building block for price and availability monitoring of permitted pages; run it as a separate service and consume its API.
entries.fit_in_engine: Price, stock and content-change alerts for brand-site and retailer pages that allow monitoring.

entries.name: PriceBuddy
entries.claimed_description: An open source, self-hostable price tracker: paste in a product URL, check it on a schedule, get notified when price or availability moves.
entries.actual_functionality: 729 files; Laravel 12, PHP 8.4, Filament admin UI; release v1.0.57; tests and CI. Per-store scrape strategies, price history, multi-store comparison, notifications, optional AI help for awkward pages (off by default).
entries.licence_note: LICENSE: GNU GPL v3; composer.json says GPL-3.0-only.
entries.popularity_note: about 1.5k GitHub stars; 80 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Not assessed in depth.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Designed for shoppers tracking arbitrary stores; no robots or terms safeguards were seen in the README.
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer tool under GPL on a different stack; useful for ideas on per-store extraction strategies.
entries.fit_in_engine: Reference only.

entries.name: PriceGhost
entries.claimed_description: Self-hosted price tracking: get notified when prices drop, hit your target price, or items come back in stock.
entries.actual_functionality: 75 files: Node/Express back end, React front end, PostgreSQL. Uses puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth, site-specific scrapers (README names Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart) and an AI fallback (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or Ollama). Version 1.0.6 (2026-01-26). No tests. README says the whole application was developed with an AI coding assistant.
entries.licence_note: No LICENSE file; the README says "MIT" in one line and package.json has no licence field; GitHub reports "not specified".
entries.popularity_note: about 1.2k GitHub stars; 28 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Stealth plugin exists to hide automation; untested code; AI keys stored by the app.
entries.external_api_dependencies: Optional LLM APIs (README: "fractions of a cent" per call).
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Stealth scraping of Amazon, Walmart and similar retailers is exactly what their terms prohibit.
entries.verdict_reason: No licence file, no tests, and built around evading bot detection on marketplaces.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.

entries.name: Discount Bandit
entries.claimed_description: A price tracker for your favorite products across multiple stores, with a built-in notification system.
entries.actual_functionality: 639 files; Laravel 12, PHP 8.4, Filament 4, headless Chromium crawler (chrome-php); release v4.0.5.
entries.licence_note: No licence file and no licence statement in the README. composer.json still carries the Laravel skeleton's own name and default "MIT" field, which is not a licence grant for this project. No licence means all rights reserved.
entries.popularity_note: about 766 GitHub stars; 10 open issues (shields.io / npm / PyPI figures retrieved 2026-11-26).
entries.security_observations: Not assessed in depth.
entries.marketplace_terms_concerns: Consumer price tracker for arbitrary stores.
entries.verdict_reason: No licence, so it cannot legally be reused.
entries.fit_in_engine: None.
